title: Composition of Memory Experts for Diffusion World Models
role: A contrastive product of experts on video models, showing what a negative expert does when it is each model's own baseline
reads: Video diffusion experts read noisy frames plus past frames, LoRA-stored history or camera poses; no text
trained_on: Pretrained video diffusion models (DiT, 150k steps on Memory Maze); long-term expert fine-tunes LoRA adapters on the current episode at test time
score_enters: Sum over experts of alpha times the conditional score plus (1 minus alpha) times that expert's baseline score, at every noise level, alpha 2 to 3 (Eq. 6)
adding_scores: Under disjoint kernels the contrastive expert keeps kernel shapes and only reweights modes (Prop 1); that assumption does not cover overlapping noised kernels or the product across experts (inferred)
unseen: no: evaluates video prediction and recall with no held-out concepts
headline: LPIPS perceptual distance 0.097 for the composition against 0.113 for full attention on Memory Maze, DiT, lower is better
copy_or_avoid: Copy the margin test and the with-and-without-negative ablation; avoid treating unconditional negatives as evidence for wrong-sentence negatives (inferred)
model: DiT, UViT and U-Net video diffusion models

disagreements.claim: The long-term expert's negative is the model with no context
disagreements.source: Eq. 4 on p. 6 prints the negative as the unadapted weights with the same context c
disagreements.paper_says: The contrastive expert is then the model without any context

disagreements.claim: Without contrast, stacking experts fails to outperform the base model

disagreements.paper_says: Without contrastive weighting, stacking multiple experts fails to outperform the base model
